sections.title: Detailed Brief Overview
rows: The **Delhi Sultanate** (दिल्ली सल्तनत) refers to the period of five successive Muslim dynasties that ruled from Delhi between **1206 AD and 1526 AD**.
Spanned across **320 years** from **1206 AD** (Accession of Qutb-ud-din Aibak) to **1526 AD** (First Battle of Panipat).
Centered in **Delhi**, extending over large parts of the Indian subcontinent (North India, parts of Deccan, and Bengal).
Ruled by five distinct dynasties: **Slave Dynasty (Mamuk)**, **Khilji Dynasty**, **Tughlaq Dynasty**, **Sayyid Dynasty**, and **Lodi Dynasty**.
Established **Islamic rule and administrative framework** in India, introduced Persian culture, Indo-Islamic architecture, and centralized revenue systems.
Introduction of **Iqta system**, construction of iconic monuments like **Qutub Minar**, market control policies, and frequent Mongol incursions.
High-scoring static GK section: Chronology, founder/last ruler names, capital shifts, revenue terms, and architectural contributions.
Official language was **Persian**, currency reforms introduced **Tanka (silver)** and **Jittal (copper)** by Iltutmish.

items.title: 1. Chronological Order of Delhi Sultanate Dynasties
items.content:
• **Slave Dynasty (1206–1290 AD):** Founded by Qutb-ud-din Aibak; also known as Mamluk or Ilbari dynasty.
• **Khilji Dynasty (1290–1320 AD):** Founded by Jalal-ud-din Khilji; marked by imperial expansion under **Alauddin Khilji**.
• **Tughlaq Dynasty (1320–1414 AD):** Founded by Ghiyas-ud-din Tughlaq; longest ruling dynasty with ambitious administrative experiments.
• **Sayyid Dynasty (1414–1451 AD):** Founded by Khizr Khan; claimed descent from Prophet Muhammad.
• **Lodi Dynasty (1451–1526 AD):** Founded by Bahlol Lodi; first **Afghan dynasty** in India, ended at Panipat.
• **Mnemonic for Dynasties:** **S**ee **K**ing **T**ake **S**eat **L**ately (Slave, Khilji, Tughlaq, Sayyid, Lodi).

items.title: 2. Slave Dynasty (Mamluk Dynasty) - Key Highlights
items.content:
• **Qutb-ud-din Aibak (1206–1210 AD):** Known as **Lakh Baksh** (giver of lakhs); started **Qutub Minar** construction; died playing Polo (Chaugan).
• **Iltutmish (1211–1236 AD):** Real consolidator of Delhi Sultanate; completed Qutub Minar; introduced **Tanka and Jittal**; organized **Turkan-i-Chahalgani** (Group of 40 nobles).
• **Razia Sultana (1236–1240 AD):** First and only **Muslim female ruler** of medieval India.
• **Ghiyas-ud-din Balban (1266–1287 AD):** Followed **Blood and Iron policy**; introduced **Sijda** (prostration) and **Paibos** (kissing feet); introduced Persian festival **Nauroz**.

items.title: 3. Khilji Dynasty and Alauddin Khilji's Reforms
items.content:
• **Jalal-ud-din Khilji (1290–1296 AD):** Founder, known for his mild and lenient administration.
• **Alauddin Khilji (1296–1316 AD):** First sultan to maintain a **permanent standing army**; introduced **cash salaries** and **branding of horses (Daag)** and **descriptive roll of soldiers (Chehra)**.
• **Market Control Policy:** Established strict price controls and appointed **Diwan-i-Riyasat** and **Shahna-i-Mandi** to check cheating and hoarding.
• **Land Revenue:** Raised land revenue to **50% of produce** (Biswa); measured land for tax assessment.
• **Mnemonic for Alauddin's Military Reforms:** **D**o **C**ash **P**ayments (Daag, Chehra, Permanent army).

items.title: 4. Tughlaq Dynasty - Experiments and Failures
items.content:
• **Ghiyas-ud-din Tughlaq (1320–1325 AD):** Built the fortified city of **Tughlaqabad**; died due to collapse of a pavilion.
• **Muhammad bin Tughlaq (1325–1351 AD):** Known as the **wise fool / mixture of opposites**; shifted capital from **Delhi to Daulatabad** (1327 AD); introduced **Token Currency** (copper coins replacing silver).
• **Agricultural Reforms:** Created a new department **Diwan-i-Kohi** for agriculture.
• **Firuz Shah Tughlaq (1351–1388 AD):** Built extensive canals for irrigation; founded cities like **Jaunpur, Hisar, Firozabad**; established **Diwan-i-Khairat** (charity department) and **Diwan-i-Banda-gan** (slaves department); levied Jizya strictly.

items.title: 5. Sayyid and Lodi Dynasties
items.content:
• **Khizr Khan (1414–1421 AD):** Founder of Sayyid dynasty; ruled as a vassal of Timur.
• **Bahlol Lodi (1451–1489 AD):** Founder of Lodi dynasty; respected Afghan nobles (called *Maqsad-i-Ali*).
• **Sikandar Lodi (1489–1517 AD):** Founded **Agra city in 1504 AD** and made it his capital; introduced **Gaj-i-Sikandari** (32 digits yard) for land measurement; wrote Persian poetry under pen name **Gulrukhi**.
• **Ibrahim Lodi (1517–1526 AD):** Last Lodi and last Delhi Sultan; arrogant ruler who alienated nobles; defeated and killed by **Babur** in the **First Battle of Panipat (1526 AD)**.

items.title: 6. Central Administration and Departments
items.content:
• **Diwan-i-Wizarat:** Department of Finance and Revenue, headed by **Wazir**.
• **Diwan-i-Ariz:** Department of Military, headed by **Ariz-ud-mumalik**.
• **Diwan-i-Insha:** Department of Royal Correspondence.
• **Diwan-i-Rasalat:** Department of Religious affairs and appeals.
• **Diwan-i-Bandagan:** Department of Slaves (created by Firuz Shah Tughlaq).
• **Provincial Administration:** Provinces were called **Iqtas**, administered by **Iqtadars** or **Muqtis**.

items.definition: **S**allu **K**a **T**ime **S**ave **L**ife stands for **S**lave, **K**hilji, **T**ughlaq, **Sayyid**, and **L**odi dynasties.
**3 D's**: **D**aag (branding horses), **D**escriptive roll (**C**hehra/Chehra), and **D**irect cash salary.
Remember **D-T-K-K-Q**: **D**aulatabad capital shift, **T**oken currency, **K**horasan expedition, **K**arajil expedition, and **Q**arachil tax hike (agricultural tax in Doab).
Think **A-G-S**: **A**gra city founded (1504), **G**aj-i-Sikandari (land unit), **S**ultan who wrote poetry as **Gulrukhi**.
**A**ibak built **Q**utub (**A**ibak **Q**utub) and **Q**uwwat-ul-Islam mosque.
**S**and **P**aper: **S**ijda (prostration) and **P**aibos (kissing feet).

items.term: Mistake 1: Founder of Qutub Minar vs Completer
items.definition: Students often think Iltutmish built Qutub Minar. **Fact:** Qutb-ud-din Aibak *started* it, but Iltutmish *completed* the first three storeys.

items.term: Mistake 2: First Muslim Woman Ruler vs Razia
items.definition: Razia Sultana is the first and only female Muslim ruler, but students confuse her with Nur Jahan or Chand Bibi of later periods.
Do not confuse Delhi to Daulatabad shift (Muhammad bin Tughlaq) with Agra foundation (Sikandar Lodi).

items.term: Mistake 4: First Battle of Panipat Participants
items.definition: Often confused with Battle of Tarain. First Battle of Panipat (1526) was between **Babur and Ibrahim Lodi**, ending the Sultanate.
Students assume token currency was gold or silver. **Fact:** It was **copper/brass** coins introduced by Muhammad bin Tughlaq to match silver value.
Lodis were **Afghans**, whereas all other four Delhi Sultanate dynasties were of **Turkic** origin.
Delhi Sultanate lasted from **1206 AD to 1526 AD** covering five dynasties.
**Qutb-ud-din Aibak** established slave rule in 1206 AD with Lahore (later Delhi) as capital.
**Iltutmish** is regarded as the real consolidator of the Delhi Sultanate.
**Ghiyas-ud-din Balban** crushed the Chahalgani and enforced strict royal despotism.
**Alauddin Khilji** implemented rigid price control and grain management.
Alauddin Khilji introduced cash payment and **Daag/Chehra** system for soldiers.
**Muhammad bin Tughlaq** shifted capital to Daulatabad in 1327 AD, causing massive hardship.
**Firuz Shah Tughlaq** focused on public works, canals, hospitals, and employment bureaus.
**Sikandar Lodi** founded modern Agra city in **1504 AD**.
The Sultanate concluded when **Ibrahim Lodi** fell in the **First Battle of Panipat (1526 AD)**.

upscNotes.content: UPSSSC PET frequently asks direct matching questions between Sultans and their unique administrative innovations (e.g., Diwan-i-Kohi, Tanka, Daag). Memorize the departments and their founders.
Focus heavily on the years 1206, 1290, 1320, 1414, 1451, and 1526. Chronology questions carry guaranteed marks in UP exams.
Trap: Examiners often trap students by asking who introduced Jizya on Brahmins for the first time. **Answer:** Firuz Shah Tughlaq. Do not confuse with Qutb-ud-din Aibak who levied it generally.
Trap: Confusing the builder of Qutub Minar. Aibak started it, but Iltutmish finished it. Read the question carefully whether it asks 'started' or 'completed'.

keyTakeaways: Five dynasties ruled the Delhi Sultanate: Slave, Khilji, Tughlaq, Sayyid, and Lodi.
Iltutmish introduced silver Tanka and copper Jittal coins.
Alauddin Khilji revolutionized military administration with Daag, Chehra, and price control.
Muhammad bin Tughlaq was known for ambitious experiments like token currency and Daulatabad shift.
Firuz Shah Tughlaq excelled in public infrastructure including canals and charity departments.
Sikandar Lodi founded Agra in 1504 AD and used Gaj-i-Sikandari for land measurement.
The Delhi Sultanate ended in 1526 AD at the First Battle of Panipat by Babur.
